Portfolio news brief — 14 September 2026

Notable price action
- Range Nuclear Renaissance ETF (NUKZ) is -5.8% over roughly three sessions (latest observed price: $62.3100).

Market and major-name developments
- Here's where they see the best income opportunities. (CNBC)
- Paul Hickey, Bespoke Investment Group co-founder, joins 'Squawk on the Street' to discuss the 10-year U.S. Treasury yield rising to a multiyear high on Monday, what it signals for the market, and more. (CNBC)
- Treasury note yield pared gains after reaching a multiyear high on Monday ahead of this week's Federal Reserve interest rate decision. The benchmark rate — which influences mortgages, auto loans and credit card debt — was last up more than 1 basis point at 4.987%. (CNBC)
- One of the more talked-about economic topics over the past year has been inflation and the Federal Reserve's (Fed) response (or lack thereof, rather). During the last Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting in July, the Fed kept rates steady for the second consecutive time under new Fed Chair Kevin Warsh. (The Motley Fool)
- The 10-Year treasury yield briefly hit 5% on Monday, peaking at 5.012%, its highest level since 2007. Rising Treasury yields reflect, above all else, that investors see inflation as entrenched over the longer term and that the Federal Reserve will have to keep the Fed funds rate elevated to rein it in. (The Motley Fool)

Costco (COST)
- If you plunk $10,000 into shares of Costco Wholesale ( COST +1.56% ) , how much passive dividend income will that generate? A cursory look at Costco would suggest its recent dividend yield of 0.65% is puny, generating just about $65 in annual income from your $10,000. (The Motley Fool)

NVIDIA (NVDA; VOO top-five holding)
- The investment bank double upgraded the artificial intelligence infrastructure stock to overweight from underweight. (CNBC)
- The growing calls for an AI slowdown, many of which coming from within the industry itself, are sending shockwaves throughout the market, sinking AI-related stocks. Meanwhile, crypto is so far unaffected, with Bitcoin today climbing—perhaps partly due to bullish regulatory news as the Clarity Act gets a second life . (Decrypt)
- Here are Monday's biggest calls on Wall Street. (CNBC)

Bitcoin (BTC)
- Strategy repurchased 1,420,467 shares of its STRC preferred stock for $139.3 million in the week to September 13, according to an 8-K filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission on Monday. That pulled back from the $176.3 million the Bitcoin treasury company spent the previous week, when its board doubled the authorization behind its digital credit securities repurchase program to $2 billion. (Decrypt)
- Bitcoin Suisse, one of the pioneers of Switzerland's Crypto Valley, is preparing to relocate up to half of the jobs at its Zug headquarters abroad as it pivots from a Swiss crypto specialist into a global wealth manager. According to an interview with Finews , the company will move as many as 60 positions overseas, with back-office and administrative roles hit hardest. (Decrypt)

Eli Lilly (LLY; XLV top-five holding)
- Novartis ( NVS +1.33% ) just reported its third clinical failure in only seven days. One of the company's pipeline setbacks triggered a ripple impact throughout one of the most hotly anticipated drug races in the biopharmaceutical industry. (The Motley Fool)

Apple (AAPL; VOO top-five holding)
- Apple on Monday released a new version of the iPhone software called iOS 27, which includes the company's redesigned Siri AI personal assistant, before the latest iPhones hit store shelves this week. The new Siri AI is in beta, Apple said, and users have to opt in through the settings app, though they may have to add their names to the waitlist before getting access. (CNBC)
- CNBC's MacKenzie Sigalos reports on the first federal court appearance between Apple and OpenAI and why the judge’s handling of discovery could shape Apple’s effort to prove OpenAI used or benefited from allegedly stolen trade secrets. (CNBC)
- Elon Musk 's X Corp and SpaceXAI said on ​Monday ​they have resolved their lawsuit in federal court in Texas that had ⁠accused ‌ Apple of conspiring to unlawfully ⁠monopolize markets for smartphones and generative AI chatbots. In a court filing, X and SpaceXAI ‌moved to dismiss the lawsuit they brought against Apple last year. (CNBC)

Microsoft (MSFT; VOO top-five holding)
- Microsoft has posted a provisional code of conduct that would impose restrictions on its artificial intelligence models, days after Anthropic and OpenAI leaders agreed to slow development speed. The company behind Windows and Office products hopes to be seen as a responsible actor in AI, where it's a prominent cloud supplier. (CNBC)

Alphabet (GOOGL; VOO top-five holding)
- Alphabet ( GOOG +3.06% ) ( GOOGL +3.22% ) has come under pressure lately as management pushes forward with its massive AI spending plans. Not only does it expect to spend around $200 billion in capital expenditures this year and significantly more next year, it also has $811 billion in purchase commitments and contractual obligations on the books, most of which it will pay by 2030. (The Motley Fool)

Informational only — verify primary sources before making investment decisions.
Routine price moves and stock-picking speculation are intentionally excluded.
